name: Ezetimibe
route_note: oral tablet once daily, alone or combined with a statin or bempedoic acid
owner: generic (many); Zetia brand held by Organon

discovery.note: Found by optimising azetidinone compounds in an animal screen before its molecular target was known.

tagline: Blocks intestinal cholesterol uptake; the usual add-on to statins
summary: Ezetimibe lowers LDL cholesterol by about 20% by blocking cholesterol absorption in the small intestine. It is used alone or with a statin, and the IMPROVE-IT trial showed that adding it to simvastatin after acute coronary syndrome modestly reduced cardiovascular events.
mechanism: Ezetimibe and its active glucuronide bind Niemann-Pick C1-Like 1 (NPC1L1), a sterol transporter on the brush border of enterocytes, blocking uptake of dietary and biliary cholesterol.
Less cholesterol reaches the liver, which responds by upregulating LDL receptors and clearing more LDL from the blood. Its effect is additive to statins, which block synthesis.
uses: Primary hypercholesterolaemia, with or without a statin

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Zetia, marketed by a Merck/Schering-Plough partnership.

history.title: Target identified
history.detail: NPC1L1 is identified as the molecular target of ezetimibe.

history.title: Vytorin
history.detail: A fixed-dose combination with simvastatin is approved.

history.title: ENHANCE controversy
history.detail: The ENHANCE imaging trial shows no reduction in carotid intima-media thickness, prompting scrutiny of delayed results.

history.title: IMPROVE-IT
history.detail: Adding ezetimibe to simvastatin after ACS reduces cardiovascular events, supporting the LDL hypothesis for non-statin therapy.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic ezetimibe becomes available in the US.

pk.metabolism: Intestinal and hepatic glucuronidation; enterohepatic recirculation

facts: Its molecular target was discovered only after the drug was already in clinical development.

references.title: Cannon CP et al. Ezetimibe added to statin therapy after acute coronary syndromes (IMPROVE-IT). N Engl J Med 2015
